summary: Nguyen Van Thuong is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Delhi, where K. T. S. Sarao served as MA supervisor.

Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) studied at Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932–1936) and under teachers including Lianju Xia, Gongga Rinpoche, and Hsu Yun. He served as head at Central People's Broadcasting Station and professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications.

Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985), who worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studied at Rissho University, Jodo Shu Daigakuin, Hōryūji Kingakuin, Kennin-ji, and other institutions. He also founded Nipponzan-Myōhōji.

Nicholas Dirks (born 1950) is a historian and Indologist who studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Chicago. He held academic posts at the California Institute of Technology (~1978–1987), University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2013).

Nicholas Justin Allen (1939–2020) was an Indologist and anthropologist who earned a BLitt and completed doctoral studies under Rodney Needham at the University of Oxford. He taught anthropology at Durham University (1972–1976) and Oxford (from 1976).

Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947) studied at Imperial St. Petersburg University and the Imperial Academy of Arts. He served as director of the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts (~1906–1917) and founded the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute.
Nicholas Witkowski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Stanford University by 2015 and served as a research fellow at the University of Tokyo (attested 2017).
Nicholson T. Collier works in religious studies and philosophy. Collier earned a PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths.

Nicola Di Cosmo (born 1957) completed a PhD at Indiana University (~1985–1991). He taught at Harvard, the University of Canterbury, and Columbia, and became Henry Luce Foundation Professor in East Asian Studies at the Institute for Advanced Study around 2003.

Nicolaas Johannes Krom (1883–1945) was an Indologist and historian. He worked at the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1913–1916) and held academic posts at Leiden University in 1919 and from 1925 to 1945.
Nicolaas van Wijk (1880–1942) was a linguist who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1898–1903) and Moscow State University (~1902–1903). He held a post at Leiden University starting in 1913.
Nicolas Morrissey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied under Gregory Schopen and holds a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and archaeology who studied at Silpakorn University and under supervisors including Claudine Bautze-Picron and Peter Skilling. He held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016).

Nicolas Tournadre (born 1959) is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed his PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Claude Hagège. He held posts at INALCO (~1995–2004) and Aix-Marseille University (~2004).
Nicole Baden (born 1981) is a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner who studied under traditional teacher Richard Baker and succeeded him in 2024.

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas (1906–1987) was a sinologist and historian. She taught Chinese art at the École du Louvre (~1958–1978) and served as professor of Chinese civilization at INALCO (~1966–1977), having previously taught at École des langues orientales.

Niels Ludvig Westergaard (1815–1878) was a Danish Indologist and linguist who studied at Copenhagen, Bonn (under Christian Lassen), Paris, London, and Oxford. At the University of Copenhagen, he served as Lektor (1844), full professor (1850), and Rektor (1867–1868).
Nigel Allan, working in Indology and history, served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine (attested 1993), succeeding Marianne Winder.

Niharranjan Ray (1903–1981) completed doctoral work at Leiden University (~1935–1936). He served as Chief Librarian (1936) and Bageswari Professor of Fine Arts (1946–1965) at the University of Calcutta, and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1965–1970).
Nika Jovic is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Vienna under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2010) and teacher Géza Bethlenfalvy (2007–2008).
